theorem_title: Gauge-fixed single-sensor kernels have arbitrarily large target values
natural_language_statement:
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and $x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb Z^2$, define the observation $r_n(x)=x_1+(n+1)x_2$, target $q(x)=x_1$, and witness $w_n=(n+1,-1)$. For every natural bound $B$, there exist $n\in\mathbb N$ and $d\in\mathbb Z^2$ such that

$$
r_n(d)=0,\qquad d_2=-1,\qquad q(d)>B.
$$

This is an exact unbounded family with fixed second coordinate. The sensor index varies with the bound; the statement does not assert a common nonzero direction for all sensors or a normalized condition-number estimate.
formal_statement:
theorem NewMathDiscovery.LinearBlindness.RankTwoInstability.unbounded_target_on_gauge_fixed_kernel (bound : Nat) :
    ∃ n direction,
      observe n direction = 0 ∧
      direction.2 = -1 ∧
      target direction > Int.ofNat bound := by sorry
